source.title: Quantifying Empirical Compute-Supervision Tradeoffs in RLVR
source.authors: Ryouya Mitsuhashi; Patrick H. Chen; Isabelle Tseng; Jasin Cekinmez; Addison J. Wu

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses scaling laws and reports compute-versus-verifier-quality results for RLVR post-training, but does not test the listed claims about held-out pretraining loss, power-law extrapolation, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or the other specified versions.
record.gate_note: The study varies GRPO rollouts and verifier noise, measuring GSM8K validation accuracy after RLVR. That is related to compute scaling, but its outcome is not held-out pretraining loss and it does not test the listed power-law or compute-optimal-allocation claims. Its results are its own, not results cited from other work.
record.test_reason: The study scales GRPO rollouts per prompt during RLVR post-training of Qwen2.5 0.5B and 1.5B on GSM8K, with injected verifier noise. It measures true validation accuracy, not held-out pretraining loss. It does not vary parameters, tokens or pretraining compute. Its compute term is a log-linear regressor fitted on only three rollout values, and the authors say they do not resolve the functional form in r. So it does not test the power-law form in a new regime (V5) or downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss (V6). Kaplan and Hoffmann appear only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. Add that Appendix C reports cases where more rollouts do compensate for verifier error, e.g. (0.3, 64) beats (0.0, 4) on the 1.5B model. Also add that the fitted optimum sits at a moderate false-positive rate with zero false negatives.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales GRPO rollout counts during RLVR post-training while varying verifier noise; the original sources study language-model pretraining loss and parameter/token/compute scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with rollout count, false-positive and false-negative rates, model size, and whether final-step or best-step validation accuracy is used. The authors also note rollout-related plateaus in some symmetric-noise cases.

fits_no_version.finding: In GRPO on GSM8K (Qwen2.5 0.5B and 1.5B), fitted accuracy has a small positive log2-rollout coefficient (0.021–0.062). Gaps from verifier noise persist across r = 8–32. With symmetric noise and r up to 64, high-rollout noisy runs sometimes beat a perfect verifier at r = 4, and plateaus appear for the 1.5B model at low noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In RLVR post-training, more rollout compute gives diminishing gains in true accuracy and only partly offsets verifier noise; false negatives hurt more than false positives.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted to the 1st Workshop on Combining Theory and Benchmarks, CTB@ICML 2026
record.problems: One seed per configuration; the authors state that compute constraints limit experiments to relatively small Qwen models. The main rollout sweep has only three values, and the paper explicitly says it does not claim to resolve the functional form in rollout count from those values. The symmetric-noise comparison values are described qualitatively without numerical accuracies.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to much larger runs.
No allocation of parameters and tokens under a fixed compute budget.
RLVR rollout scaling is fitted log-linearly on three points. No power-law form is tested for post-training.
GSM8K accuracy is not related to model scale or to pretraining loss; the only axis varied is rollout count.
No comparison of fitting choices for pretraining laws. The study notes only limitations of its own polynomial fit.

record.verdict_notes: One seed per configuration and only three rollout values in the main sweep. 'Scaling laws' here means rollout-compute regressions in RL post-training, not loss scaling laws.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure held-out pretraining loss against parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Does not fit power laws on small runs and test predictions on much larger runs.
Does not vary parameter and token counts under a fixed compute budget or estimate their compute-optimal growth.
Does not compare architectures at fixed parameter count.
Studies RLVR post-training, but does not test whether the same power-law form for held-out loss applies in that regime or another modality.
Measures GSM8K validation accuracy during post-training, not downstream-task performance predicted from scale or pretraining loss.
Does not test dependence of the original loss-law exponents or compute-optimal split on fitting choices; it notes limitations of its own compute fit.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 1.5B
rows.operation_detail: Fit validation accuracy as a second-order polynomial in false-positive and false-negative rates plus a log2-rollout term; aggregate fit across the sampled configurations.
rows.measure: Fitted validation accuracy surface; compute coefficient is +0.0344 log2 r.
rows.locator: Section 4, Scaling observations on 1.5B model; Figure 4
rows.note: The paper says increasing rollouts improves performance across noise levels but does not eliminate noise-induced gaps. This is validation accuracy in RLVR, not a test of a listed version.
